what_it_does: High-performance computing clusters face conflicting requirements: they must be stable for production workloads, customizable for diverse research needs, and reproducible so experiments can be repeated. Traditional HPC software stacks are large monolithic packages that cannot satisfy all these needs. This paper proposes decomposing the containerization architecture into five separate concerns: how to specify and build environments (using Spack and continuous integration), how to provision computing sessions (using PAM and Kubernetes), how to integrate with schedulers like Slurm, how to manage system-level integration, and how to enforce security policies.
